name: sarcasm
quote: That's a top-performing organization, I tell you.
description: A statement that is intended to mean the opposite of the literal meaning, signaling negativity about something with a touch of humor.

variations.name: perceived sarcasm
variations.description: Detecting sarcasm involves physical perceptions like tone of voice, comparing the literal meaning of words within their context, and perhaps knowing something of the speaker's habits and beliefs. You may react to perceived sarcasm with experiences including humor, annoyance, contempt, or anger depending on the context and perceptions about the speakers intentions.

comparisons.description: Sarcasm and irony both point out something that's the opposite of what's expected, but irony is meant to be more of an observation than carrying a negative editorial message.

commentaries.quote: Sarcasm helps me overcome the harshness of the reality we live, eases the pain of scars and makes people smile.
Sarcasm I now see to be, in general, the language of the Devil; for which reason I have, long since, as good as renounced it.
The subconscious doesn't distinguish sarcasm and jokes. It just accepts what it hears. That's the power of words.
Enjoyment of sarcasm may be driven by a sense of disappointment with the world, boredom, and/or the novelty perceived from a witty statement.

conditions: A statement that is intended to mean the opposite of the literal meaning, signaling negativity about something.
Trying to soften the message with a touch of humor.
